Date: 2026-08-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Candescent pilot — request for consolidated quarterly invoicing + escrow holdback

Rishi / Marissa,

Following today's call with Candescent Labs (Ava + Michael), they asked if we can do a temporary billing cadence for their 6-month pilot: one consolidated invoice per quarter (instead of monthly) and a small milestone-based holdback that would be escrowed until delivery of Milestone 2. They are a strategic prospect for our healthcare segment and want reduced AP cycles as they align internal approvals.

Proposal from Candescent: consolidated quarterly invoice, Net-90 for each invoice, and a 10% holdback placed in escrow until Milestone 2 acceptance. Pilot ARR would be ~$160k total over 6 months. They asked if Redwood can provide this as a one-time accommodation for the pilot only.

Key asks for approval/feedback:
- Can Finance accept consolidated quarterly invoicing for pilots (Net-90) with an escrowed 10% holdback?
- If yes, what controls do we need (PO, cap on outstanding exposure, SOC2 evidence, payment method)?
- Any mandatory contract language or required insurance / payment vehicle?

I attached the draft redlines they sent plus a short exposure estimate. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-08-25T10:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Candescent pilot — request for consolidated quarterly invoicing + escrow holdback

Jordan —

Thanks for the heads-up. A few quick points from Deal Desk / Finance:
1) Net-90 is high exposure given no prior relationship; we typically cap one-off extended terms to customers with a credit check and a signed PO.
2) Escrow/holdback for milestones is workable if legal approves language and we have a clear acceptance criteria for Milestone 2. We will need a signed SOW and an explicit acceptance workflow.
3) Exposure cap — recommend a hard cap of $200k outstanding receivable for the pilot.
4) Payment preference: ACH or wire only for extended terms (no credit card).

Please confirm: is the $160k total the full exposure at any one time or spread across two quarter invoices? Also attach the draft SOW if available. Without these, I can't approve Net-90 today.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Deal Desk & Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

> 3) Exposure cap — recommend a hard cap of $200k outstanding receivable for the pilot.

Rishi — appreciate the quick guidance. A few clarifications from my side (commercial):
- The $160k is the total contract value for the 6-month pilot. They propose two quarterly invoices: Q1 = $90k, Q2 = $70k (usage-based adjustments possible). So max outstanding at any one time is ~$90k before invoicing — below your suggested cap.
- Candescent has limited procurement bandwidth and asked for consolidated quarterly billing to reduce PO churn. They are comfortable with ACH/wire, and procurement@candescentlabs.com confirmed they will issue a PO if we can accept quarterly invoices.
- The 10% holdback (~$16k) is to be escrowed and released on Milestone 2 acceptance; they agreed to clear acceptance criteria in the SOW.

Attached: redlines from their counsel and a brief workbook showing invoice timing and exposure by month. From a sales perspective this is low risk (pilot, limited ARR), and it materially shortens procurement friction which unlocks future expansion.

If Finance still needs an exec exception, can Jordan escalate to leadership for one-time approval? We would include the PO, SOC2 evidence, ACH payment, explicit SOW acceptance conditions, and a $200k max exposure clause.

—Marissa

Jordan / Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for laying this out. I approve a one-time executive exception on the following conditional basis: 
1) Limited to this 6-month pilot only; clause to expire automatically at contract end.
2) $200k maximum outstanding exposure cap enforced by Finance (no exceptions).
3) Signed PO on file and ACH/wire as the payment method; no card.
4) Escrow/holdback language to be reviewed and signed off by Legal (we release escrow only after documented acceptance criteria for Milestone 2).
5) Require SOC2 Type II report (most recent) or equivalent security attestation before first invoice.
6) Finance to run a quick vendor credit check; if any red flags, exception rescinded.

Rishi — please implement the cap and controls into the billing profile and confirm you are comfortable operationally. Marissa / Jordan — proceed to get the PO/SOW finalized and route for DocuSign; Legal will take a quick look at the escrow text.

If everything is captured as above, approving now so we can keep the momentum.
